# Exact reverse-RLD radius for classical-input quantum-output channels

## Statement for faithful quantum outputs

Let a classical-input quantum-output channel prepare density matrices sigma_i>0 on C^d for input i=1,...,m. The sigma_i need not commute. Consider the complete conditional RLD/Petz-chi-square excess coefficient: arbitrary finite reference dimension, faithful baseline blocks R_i summing to I, Hermitian tangents H_i, and subtraction of the untouched reference contribution. Input pairs may have unequal reference marginals.

Its exact value is

C = min_{U=U*} max_i Tr[(sigma_i-U)sigma_i^-1(sigma_i-U)]
  = 1-min_{p in Delta_m} Tr[(sum_i p_i sigma_i^-1)^-1]
  = 1-1/K,

where

K=min_{omega>=0, Tr omega=1} max_i Tr[omega sigma_i^-1 omega].

Thus the proposed reverse quantum chi-square radius is correct for faithful outputs, even when they do not commute. The same constant is sharp for the operator-valued reference defect. Reference dimension at most min(m,d^2)-1 suffices in the supremum for a nonconstant channel; the physical lower witness needs no additional coherent flag. Constant channels have coefficient zero.

This theorem does not include singular outputs without a separate support convention and proof. It is a mathematical derivation, not a literature-priority claim.

## 1. The physical conditional defect

Let A=sum_i sigma_i tensor R_i and J=sum_i sigma_i tensor H_i, K=sum_i H_i. Put Z_i=H_i-R_i K, so sum Z_i=0. The output centered matrix is

Z=sum_i sigma_i tensor Z_i=J-A(I_d tensor K).

Since Tr_output A=I and Tr_output J=K, expansion gives

Tr_output[J A^-1 J]-K^2=Tr_output[Z* A^-1 Z].

The input conditional defect is sum_i Z_i*R_i^-1 Z_i. Therefore an inequality between these two positive operator-valued forms proves the physical upper bound. Reference congruence handles baseline blocks summing to arbitrary W>0 without changing dimension.

## 2. Noncommutative weighted Cauchy gives the upper bound

For positive A_i and arbitrary B_i, matrix weighted Cauchy says

(sum B_i)*(sum A_i)^-1(sum B_i)<=sum B_i*A_i^-1 B_i.

Apply it with

A_i=sigma_i tensor R_i,
B_i=(sigma_i-U) tensor Z_i.

f_i(U)=Tr[(sigma_i-U)*sigma_i^-1(sigma_i-U)].

# Quantum output erasure and ordinary complete estimation order

## Statement and definitions

Let the classical-input quantum-output channel prepare faithful density matrices sigma_i on a d-dimensional output. Let E_q reveal the classical input with probability q and otherwise erase it. With arbitrary finite untouched quantum references, its exact reveal threshold for ordinary, unsmoothed complete SLD and binary quadratic-MMSE dominance is

C = 1 - min_(p in Delta_m) Tr[(sum_i p_i sigma_i^-1)^-1].

Thus q >= C is necessary and sufficient for E_q to have no larger optimal squared-error risk for every binary encoding. It is also sufficient for every real-valued ensemble with finite second moment. “Ordinary, unsmoothed complete” describes order without Hermitian smoothing while still permitting arbitrary references. It does not mean reference-free order.

For a joint Hermitian output/reference observable A, define Phi_sigma(A)=Tr_output[(sigma tensor I)A]. This is a Hermitian reference observable.

The SLD form is g_B(H)=Tr[H L_B^-1(H)], L_B(X)=(BX+XB)/2. For centered labels its quadratic-risk dictionary and general-POVM reduction are proved in CLASSICAL_OPERATIONAL.md, Section 3. The RLD radius is defined in CQ_THEOREM.md. The proof below equates these unrestricted erasure thresholds; it does not identify SLD and RLD metrics or their fixed-reference-dimension coefficients.

## Independently reconstructed scope

The theorem in CQ_THEOREM.md has been independently reconstructed for faithful prepared states. The harmonic dual, small complex SDP, operator upper bound, physical Hermitian frame lower bound, sufficient reference dimension min(m,d²)−1, and tensor-product consequence are valid. This is an internally established mathematical result; external review and historical priority remain open. Singular prepared states remain outside this theorem.

# A support-exact reconstruction of the CQ reverse-radius theorem

Author: worker gb_reverse_genesis, 16 October 2026. Status: internal proof; no external review, formal verification, or historical priority certification.

This closes an endpoint explicitly omitted by the supplied faithful-output packet. It is also a direct independent reconstruction of a CQ consequence already latent in Astra's broader internal N402 Choi candidate. It is not claimed to be a new theorem in the literature or new to Astra's full archive. The proof below does not assume that broader candidate.

## 1. Exact statement and support convention

Let a classical input i in {1,...,m} prepare a density matrix sigma_i >= 0 on a finite-dimensional output Q. Set

    S = intersection_i range(sigma_i),
    V = span_i range(sigma_i),
    P_S = orthogonal projection onto S,
    G_i = (P_S sigma_i^+ P_S)|_S.

Here + is the Moore-Penrose inverse, and every G_i is positive definite on S when S is nonzero. For p in the FULL simplex Delta_m define

    G_p = sum_i p_i G_i,
    h(p) = Tr_S G_p^-1.

When S={0}, set h(p)=0. Crucially S is the intersection for ALL channel inputs, including inputs with p_i=0. A boundary p is the continuous extension of strictly positive priors with this fixed S. Replacing S by the support intersection of only the positive-prior inputs changes the answer.

For faithful reference blocks R_i>0 summing to I_R and Hermitian H_i, put

    K = sum_i H_i,
    A = sum_i sigma_i tensor R_i,
    J = sum_i sigma_i tensor H_i.

All output inverses are taken on V tensor R; A is strictly positive there. Define the conditional RLD input and output costs by

    E = sum_i Tr H_i R_i^-1 H_i - Tr K^2,
    N = Tr J A^-1 J - Tr K^2.

The unrestricted complete conditional coefficient is the supremum N/E over finite references and E>0. Equivalently one may permit arbitrary positive reference marginal W and subtract Tr K W^-1 K. The usual congruence removes W without enlarging the reference dimension.

Then

      = 1 - min_{p in Delta_m} h(p).                         (1)
